p: Station Hill puts you right at the heart of Reading, which means the town's best bits are a short wander away. Forbury Gardens is a lovely green spot guarded by the huge Maiwand Lion, and right next door are the Reading Abbey ruins, where King Henry I was buried. The Abbey Quarter reopened to visitors after major conservation work, and it makes a peaceful contrast to an evening of flying darts.

Reading Museum is worth a look too. Among other things it holds a full-size Victorian replica of the Bayeux Tapestry, which is a real surprise to find in a Berkshire town. For food and shops, The Oracle sits along the River Kennet with plenty of places to eat by the water.

Transport-wise, this is about as easy as it gets. Reading station is on the Elizabeth line as well as main-line routes, so groups can arrive from central London, Oxford, Bristol and beyond without needing a car.
Bigger groups should book early, as a single oche only holds so many players and splitting a party across two is easier to arrange in advance.

Allow a couple of hours if you're eating as well as playing, and get there a touch early. If darts is new to you, stand side-on, keep your elbow still and follow through. The rest is just luck and banter.
